data.why: The repo ships no example data, and _read_export_bytes reads comma-delimited CSVs as a single tab-delimited column before ever trying the comma branch, so the test files must be genuinely tab-delimited (as a real CFX Maestro text export would be) rather than .csv, with Tm, double-peak, flat-NTC, missing-value and weak-signal wells for the QC workflow.

goals: Upload a raw melt curve RFU export and see every well's melt curve plotted together
Toggle between raw RFU and -d(RFU)/dT to read each sample's Tm from the derivative peak
Upload a Peak Results file to label wells by sample name instead of bare well IDs
Search and select a subset of wells to compare side by side on the plot
Spot problem wells: a flat no-template control, a well with a double melt peak (mixed products or primer-dimer), a well with a missing data point, and a weak-signal well

review.summary: The tree fits the app's purpose: it loads Bio-Rad CFX melt exports, labels wells by sample, overlays melt curves and peaks, reads Tm and spots NTC, double-peak, missing-point and weak wells, and the screens I checked support the nodes except the PNG export. Before filing, it needs the derivative checkbox redescribed as declaring the input file type, bug workarounds taken out of the task steps, the download evidence fixed, and the export reader added as a feature.
